lanes.name: planar
lanes.focus: Planar box booleans. Start with disjoint subtraction, then containment, then touching solids along a face, an edge and a vertex, then thin and near-coincident overlaps. Derive a repair that applies to arbitrary valid solids in the supported API, not a box-specific recognizer. Separate bodies that touch along an edge or a vertex must come back as separate closed shells.

lanes.name: revolve
lanes.focus: Revolved solids. A closed profile wire with both ends on the axis, revolved a full turn, must give one closed shell with the right volume and area. Find why the remaining case comes back with the wrong volume and fix the construction or the tessellation of the faces that meet the axis, not the checker.

lanes.name: fillet
lanes.focus: Constant-radius round fillet of one vertical box edge. The mass properties already match; the result fails the kernel's own geometric consistency check, so the fillet surface, its trimming curves or the neighbouring trimmed faces disagree with each other. Make the B-rep consistent without loosening the check.

lanes.name: curved
lanes.focus: Booleans with cylindrical faces: equal-radius cylinder pairs at every centre distance including coincident, tangent and barely separated, and a through hole in a box. Intersection curves between a plane and a cylinder and between two cylinders must close, and the hole result must be one shell of genus one.

lanes.name: step
lanes.focus: STEP import of a public NIST assembly returns no solids although the file holds them. Follow the assembly traversal and the manifold solid B-rep conversion and make the import produce shells and triangles.
